verdict.rationale: Notte's own Playwright docs say sessions expose a Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint that existing Playwright code can connect to, which delivers the core of bringing existing automation to Notte browsers. The evidence is a single documentation line with no Puppeteer example, no connection or compatibility details, and no hands-on confirmation, so full coverage is not shown. missing for 10: explicit Puppeteer connection documentation, details on CDP endpoint usage and compatibility limits, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can connect my existing Playwright, Puppeteer, or CDP automation code to the product's browsers instead of rewriting it

citations.quote: Notte sessions expose a Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) endpoint that you can connect to with Playwright.
Sessions are isolated browser instances running in the cloud that you can control programmatically.
